entry.title: A new style of blog post

link.title: A new style of blog post

entry.content:
I recently sought to bring life to this blog. Unfortunately, I found that I too easily fell into the trap of over editing, to the point that my posts lost my voice.

And so, I have made the radical decision to write my posts by hand. I recently got a new fountain pen, and I have found writing cursive with it on nice paper to have brought back an enjoyment of writing in me that I had long since thought forgotten.

Enjoy these unadulterated windows into my mind.
entry.summary: Handwritten posts, a fountain pen, and writing without over-editing.

entry.title: On passion
entry.content:
I’ve spent much of my free time this past week at a paper store learning about paper. What a joy it must be to run a store for something you love so much. I hope for a similar thing for my future.

I’ve always loved people who genuinely love their work. Perhaps that is why I ended up at a school with the motto My heart is in the work! Despite all the criticism that statement gets, I do find it to be a beautiful notion.

What a joy it is to be utterly and irrevocably in love with your work and how lucky I am to be able to feel such a joy.
entry.summary: A paper store, a school motto, and being in love with your work.

entry.title: On knowledge
entry.content:
I have always loved learning. If I had to summarize what I am most passionate about in one word, that word would be learning.

Today I walked out of a meeting for my job and walked out smiling with the wonder of a child. My teammates all asked such interesting questions. It made me feel so joyous to be surrounded by so many people who were so intelligent, but greater than that, so curious. I feel so lucky to be able to learn from such people.

I have for a while now been mulling over my future, and I think the biggest question was built around the PhD. I believe I have been approaching this question entirely incorrectly. A PhD is a doctorate in philosophy. I take philosophy here to mean a curiosity of all that is around, within, and above us.

It’s so incredible that I have this opportunity to spend 6 years being curious about the world around me. Obviously, it doesn’t stop there. It seems to me that a scientist’s job is put simply to be curious about the world around them.

What an exciting life!
entry.summary: Curiosity, the company of the curious, and what a PhD actually is.

entry.title: On leisure
entry.content:
Aristotle believed leisure to be the ultimate goal of human life. To our modern sensibilities this may seem odd, but here it is important to perhaps think deeper.

The word school traces its origins to the Greek word schole. Schole translating to leisure. I quite appreciate this framing. It requires a certain level of freedom to pursue an education and we who have received one are so lucky to have been able to do so.

I appreciate seeing the implications of this idea. It is unfortunate, but many of history’s examples of leisure are often built on the oppression of others. However, I don’t believe this is a necessary condition.

Assuming this is true, we can begin to stumble on an exciting world of possibilities. We can enter a model where those with the soul of an artist would be fully freed to practice their art, those with the soul of a craftsman their craft, and those with the soul of a scientist their science.

I believe this to be a fascinating possibility to which we must remain open.
entry.summary: Schole, education, and a world where artists, craftsmen, and scientists are free to practice.
